item.description:

Short Description:
Modular inputs for open UK datasets, with a configuration UI. Ingests UK Carbon Intensity (api.carbonintensity.org.uk — half-hourly national intensity + generation mix) and NHS England monthly A&E attendance statistics. No API key. Idempotent, checkpoint-based, safe to run on any interval.


Description:
**UK Open Data** is a UCC-framework built add-on that brings two well-known open UK datasets into Splunk with no API key and no external dependencies beyond outbound HTTPS. **Carbon Intensity** — polls the National Grid ESO Carbon Intensity API (`api.carbonintensity.org.uk`) and indexes, per half-hourly settlement period, the national forecast/actual gCO₂/kWh and intensity band (`carbonintensity:national`) plus the generation mix by fuel type (`carbonintensity:generation`). Ideal for carbon-aware scheduling, ESG dashboards and "greenest time to run" decisions. **NHS A&E (monthly)** — scans the NHS England "A&E Attendances and Emergency Admissions" pages, downloads each monthly CSV you haven't already loaded, and indexes one event per provider plus a national TOTAL row (`nhs:ae:monthly`) — type 1/2/other attendances, 4-hour performance and over-4hr counts. Great for healthcare performance and public-sector analytics. Both inputs are **idempotent**: they checkpoint what they've already indexed, so they're safe to run on any interval without creating duplicates. Carbon re-emits only un-settled recent periods until their actual value lands; NHS only loads months it hasn't seen. Built with the Splunk UCC framework — full configuration UI, per-input index/interval settings, and standard logging.

Full history: [https://github.com/Reallysec/RST-AI-Copilot-for-Splunk/releases](https://github.com/Reallysec/RST-AI-Copilot-for-Splunk/releases)


Short Description:
AI copilot for Splunk Enterprise: plain-language questions become runnable SPL with results and an explanation; events are explained; alerts are triaged and investigated (licensed). Bring your own OpenAI-compatible or on-prem model. Data is masked before any prompt leaves the instance.


Description:
RST AI Copilot for Splunk brings an AI assistant into Splunk Enterprise for security and IT operations teams. Ask a question in plain English or Chinese and get runnable SPL with the result table, an explanation of what the search does, and a confidence level. Paste or select events to have them explained. Field names, indexes and sourcetypes come from your own data, so the generated searches use the fields you actually have. It answers a common problem: analysts know what they want to find but not the exact SPL, fields or data models, and alert queues grow faster than they can be worked. You bring the model. Any OpenAI-compatible endpoint works, including a self-hosted model on your own network. Nothing leaves the instance until an administrator configures an endpoint, and field masking (cloud / private / air-gapped modes) replaces sensitive values before a prompt is sent. The free Community Edition covers natural language to SPL, log explanation, the field dictionary, a data onboarding assistant, the | copilot and | splexplain search commands, a security posture page, baseline checks over the Splunk CIM, a runbook knowledge base, audit logging and role-based access. A licence key unlocks alert triage and investigation, the detection-rule copilot, platform health, noise reduction and scheduled reports; Enterprise adds ES Incident Review write-back, ticketing, an MCP server, audit forwarding and model failover. Short Description:

Description:
A second opinion for Splunk Enterprise Security findings. For each finding, the app collects the surrounding facts with SPL (asset and identity, Exposure Analytics, threat intelligence and network owner, related findings, risk details, CIM data models, CloudTrail, endpoint and GuardDuty data) and asks a decision model — TypeSafe Jev by default — for a suggested disposition (True Positive, False Positive, Benign or Undetermined) and a suggested urgency (Critical, High, Medium or Low). Answers below the confidence threshold, or that change when the options are asked in reverse order, become Undetermined instead of a guess. Suggestions only: the app never changes a finding or an investigation. Analysts make the final call in Enterprise Security. The suggestion is shown next to the ES AI SOC Analyst result, an LLM of your choice can explain it in plain language, and it can be written to the finding or its investigation as a Note. item.title: Splunk MCP Server - v2.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
**Splunk MCP Server 2.2.0** Splunk MCP Server 2.2.0 adds tools for running and managing asynchronous searches, pagination for additional tools, and new search options. It also updates token and encryption key defaults, improves governance visibility, and expands client compatibility. **What's New** **Asynchronous Search** Added three tools for managing long-running searches: * splunk_submit_query * splunk_get_query_results * splunk_cancel_query Use these tools to submit a search, check its status, retrieve paginated results, and cancel the search. Now, search results are retained for 30 minutes by default. Both *splunk_run_query* and *splunk_submit_query* support a *keep_results_minutes* parameter for setting retention from 1 minute to 7 days. **Pagination Changes** Added pagination to the following tools: * splunk_get_user_list * splunk_get_metadata * splunk_get_kv_store_collections * splunk_get_knowledge_objects * splunk_get_query_results Paginated alert and sourcetype tools also follow the configured maximum row limit. Increased the default maximum row limit from 1,000 to 50,000 and the default row limit from 100 to 10,000. The max row limit parameter is now configurable by the authorized users. **Search Improvements** * Added optional event sampling to *splunk_run_query*. Responses include the sampling ratio, and aggregate results reflect the sampled data. * Added fast, smart, and verbose search modes to *splunk_run_query* and *splunk_submit_query*. The default is smart mode. * Added scan count and event count to successful *splunk_run_query* responses. * Updated SPL validation to use the specified app context. **Discovery Improvements** * Added the search time range and SPL query to *splunk_get_sourcetypes* responses. * Added *splunk_server* to *splunk_get_knowledge_objects* responses. **Token Management and Governance** * Changed the default validity for new tokens to 30 days and for new encryption keys from 180 days to 90 days. * Added a panel to Access & Governance showing the 20 most recent token and encryption key changes. * Added *mcp_edit_tokens_own* to the capability dashboard and a search-head filter to the Usage dashboard. **MCP and Client Compatibility** * Updated built-in tool schemas for OpenAI strict-mode tool calling and updated MCP ping responses. * Increased the default timeout for Splunk REST API requests from 60 seconds to 120 seconds. **Upgrade Considerations** * New tokens and encryption keys use the updated default validity periods unless another supported duration is specified. Tokens cannot outlive the encryption key. * The newly paginated SPL tools rerun their search for each page. For a consistent result set, use *splunk_submit_query* and *splunk_get_query_results*. * Pagination is limited to the configured maximum row limit. Automatic pagination does not apply to custom tools, *splunk_run_query*, or *splunk_run_saved_search*. * Canceling an asynchronous search removes the search job and its cached results. Retrieve any needed results before canceling. * Keep the MCP *max_row_limit* at or below *\[restapi] maxresultrows* in *limits.conf*. A higher MCP limit can cause truncated results to appear complete.


Description:
MCP Server for Splunk Platform The Model Context Protocol (MCP) is an open standard and framework that enables seamless, secure, and standardized two-way communication between AI applications (like large language models) and external data sources or tools. It acts as a universal adapter allowing AI systems to access, execute, and integrate functionalities from diverse systems through a common protocol, simplifying data sharing and tool interoperability without custom coding for each integration. Splunk's Model Context Protocol (MCP) server leverages this to provide a standardized, secure, and scalable interface to connect AI assistants, agents, and other intelligent systems with data in the Splunk platform for both Enterprise & Cloud customers in beta. 🔑 Key Features - Universal Connectivity Seamlessly connects AI agents and tools to Splunk data resources in a secure and efficient manner. - Enterprise-Grade Security Includes built-in authentication, authorization, and Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). - Rapid Deployment Offers a plug-and-play solution, eliminating the need for custom integrations. ⚙️ Core Capabilities - Explore the Data Navigate and interact with Splunk data effortlessly. - Discover Knowledge Objects Identify and access relevant saved searches, lookups, and other knowledge assets. - Execute Searches Run powerful Splunk queries to extract insights and drive intelligent workflows. - Leverage AI capabilities from Splunk’s AI Assistant for SPL & MLTK SPL search generation from natural language, search optimization, search explanation, retrieve MLTK models and algorithms.

item.title: Log10x App - v1.3.1 [New App Release]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
\- The app opens on Overview: compact events for the chosen time range, the event text volume they save and the reduction, per index and source type. A row opens a \`tx\` search of that source. \- Health replaces Diagnostics: six checks, from compact events arriving to every event expanding, including that a search returns the same event as was indexed. \- The app's navigation holds four pages: Overview, Health, Search and Alerts. \- Through \`txf\`, an alias of a field that only a lookup sets equals raw, empty where the raw event has none, such as the Windows add-on's \`category\` and the FortiGate add-on's \`vendor_transport\`.


Short Description:
Send Splunk the logs that sampling and filters keep out to fit the license, on that same license. Compact events take a fraction of the volume and expand back byte-identical at search time; classic dashboards keep their SPL, and one command covers the search bar, saved searches, alerts and the REST API.


Description:
With the Log10x App, Splunk can index compact log events and still search, chart and alert on the original lines. The 10x Receiver stores each event as a template hash plus the values that change, so a stream of repeated patterns takes less of the license. On the OpenTelemetry demo, Splunk's license meter counted 63.91% fewer bytes, encoded events and templates included, and every line expanded back byte-identical with the Receiver settings in the installation steps (measurement: https://github.com/log-10x/benchmarks/tree/main/splunk-license). The same license then holds more: sources that were sampled, filtered or kept out of Splunk to stay under the limit can come back, or the license can be smaller. To search by what the lines say, write the tx macro in front of an ordinary search: index=my_index `tx` "payment failed" NOT retry. It runs as native SPL in the search bar, Dashboard Studio, saved searches and alerts, and NOT, OR, groups, phrases, field conditions, and values such as IP addresses and hostnames behave as they do on the original data. Classic dashboards keep their SPL: the browser sends each panel's search to the app, which rewrites it on the server. An alert created in the app's Compile Alert view is compiled once into a native saved search. The 10x Receiver produces compact events, and it is free on up to 10 nodes (https://www.log10x.com/pricing). No sign-up is required: with no license token it runs the full product on up to 10 nodes, air-gapped, with no expiry (https://doc.log10x.com/manage/license/). Preserve local notification settings and alert action configuration. For read-only notification diagnostics: ``` | makeresults | lcmnotificationstatus ``` ## Validation * 641 Python regression tests passed. * Python syntax, JavaScript, XML, and configuration validation passed. * Dashboard Studio validation passed. * Successfully validated in the LAB environment. * Native Search Head Cluster failover and concurrent-delivery scenarios require environment-specific verification before production deployment. ## Known Limitations * Legacy monitoring records without a previously persisted numeric `last_event_epoch` may require a new event or verified correction. * Uncertain SMTP delivery outcomes require reconciliation and are not automatically resent. * High-volume environments should validate monitoring-search performance and result completeness. * Mixed-version Search Head Cluster deployments are not certified. **Version:** 1.2.9 **Release Status:** LAB Validated — Controlled Production Rollout Recommended

item.title: MCP Watch - v1.2.0 [Version Update]
item.description:
Platform: Splunk


Release Notes:
MCP-Watch 1.2.0 Detection overhaul. MCP traffic is now identified from the provenance stamp the Splunk MCP Server writes to \_audit (provenance\="MCP:\:\"), so the official server works out of the box with no lookup editing. NEW \- Provenance-based detection: every MCP query is tagged with its server and tool, whatever account it runs under. \- Real time windows: the time range is read from the audit event (apiStartTime/apiEndTime), so ranges the MCP server passes as API parameters are scored correctly. \- Query cost: result count, events scanned and run time per query, plus a "Most expensive queries" panel. \- MCP server telemetry on the Activity dashboard: tool latency, rejected logins by source IP, SPL refused by the server's safety check. \- Alert: Unlisted MCP Account (MCP queries from an account not in mcp_users.csv). \- Alert: MCP Authentication Failures (5 or more rejected logins per source IP within 15 minutes). \- Access matrix shows actual tool use, including tools that the deny policy forbids but an account called anyway. CHANGED \- Six dashboards consolidated into four: Overview, Activity, Risk, Access. Bookmarks to the remaining views keep working. \- Alerts are per-result with per-user suppression and non-overlapping 5-minute windows. \- The four reports are no longer scheduled. Nothing read their results; re-enable scheduling locally if you e-mail them. \- Objects are no longer exported globally (export \= system removed). FIXED \- Wide-time, wildcard-index (index\="\*", index IN (\*), index\=\_\*) and export/delete detections that missed MCP traffic. \- The "more than 100k results" risk bonus never fired. \- Liveness status was global instead of per MCP server. \- Distributed deployments: REST calls pinned to the local search head; indexer-side remote\_\* audit copies excluded so queries are not counted twice. (not yet verified on a cluster) \- Index scope now includes inherited indexes; telemetry fields are no longer double-counted. UPGRADE NOTES \- If your own searches append earliest\= or user\= directly after the mcp_audit_searches macro, move the time range to the dispatch settings and filter with "| search user\=...". \- The "no time bound" flag now has weight 3, so expect "Risky queries %" to change. Also includes the 1.1.x releases: multi-signal detection (user agent + endpoint), liveness heartbeats, a unified Access & Tools view, and dashboard correctness fixes. AppInspect (precert, cloud tags): 0 failures. Self-test: 80/80 fixtures pass. Full changelog: [https://github.com/ALPERKESKE/mcp-watch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/ALPERKESKE/mcp-watch/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)


Short Description:
Tracks AI agent activity in Splunk by analyzing _audit and _internal logs to surface MCP server queries, flag anti-patterns, and report REST endpoint usage.


Description:
MCP-Watch provides visibility and governance for AI agents operating against Splunk through the Model Context Protocol. The app surfaces every SPL query executed by MCP servers, flags anti-patterns such as wildcard index searches and overly wide time ranges, and reports on REST endpoint usage. It reads exclusively from Splunk's built-in _audit and _internal indexes, requiring no additional data ingestion or dependencies. Administrators configure a lookup table with the Splunk usernames their MCP servers authenticate as, and the app then tracks query volume, identifies quality issues, and enables per-user tool access governance. Four dashboards present MCP activity across operational and compliance dimensions, while scheduled searches and alerts provide ongoing monitoring of agent behavior.

Everything since 1.1.0. **Hosts** - Hosts sending, silent and new for every log and index, Find a host, and host issues and alerts when hosts stop sending. **Alerts and issues** - Silent-log, host and root cause alerts follow each issue's state. A snoozed or suppressed issue sends no alert; when a snooze ends the issue opens again and alerts if the problem is still there. - A suppressed over-firing rule comes back when its alerts a day double. - An alert reaches each channel once; a channel that was down gets it when it is back. **Trust and access** - Every record is shown only to people whose Splunk roles can search the indexes it is about, including run history, collector health and approvals. - Every write goes through the Vyrux service and is checked for the person before it is saved. A stale page cannot undo a colleague's change. - Approvals cover the exact content asked for and what it replaces, for rules, parsers and suppressions. - Parser plans cannot set Splunk's own fields (host, index, source, sourcetype, _time). **Rule checks** - A search Splunk stops at its time limit is an error, never a count of zero. - The intent check reads names with fewer false readings and proves each mismatch with the rule's own events. - Macro arguments are filled in the same way everywhere, so no index is hidden in a macro. **Background scan** - One failing stage no longer stops the scan. Upgrades from earlier builds are applied once per build, and any failure is shown on System health. Full notes: the Release notes page in the Vyrux guide.


Short Description:
Know your Splunk security monitoring works. Vyrux checks that your logs arrive, your detection rules can fire and your ATT&CK coverage is real.


Description:
Your SOC depends on three things every day: the logs arrive, the logs parse, and the detection rules can fire. When one of them breaks, Splunk does not tell you. You find out after an incident, when the alert you expected never came. Vyrux checks all three every 15 minutes, inside your own Splunk. When a log stops arriving, Vyrux opens an issue, names the detection rules that can no longer fire, and alerts your team in Microsoft Teams, Slack or email. When a rule cannot fire, Vyrux says why: a missing field, macro, lookup or data model, a search window shorter than the log's delay, or scheduled runs that never finish. It also says who owns the fix. When many rules break for one reason, such as a firewall upgrade that changes the log format, Vyrux shows the one cause and the one fix that restores them all. Your MITRE ATT&CK coverage is measured from rules that actually work, not from rules that merely exist. Vyrux then helps your engineers fix what it finds, with Parsing Studio, a rule intent check, a Tuning Lab and Chuka, an optional AI detection engineer. Nothing changes in Splunk until a person deploys it, and you can require a second person to approve each change first. Vyrux is a Splunk app, not a SaaS service. It runs on your search head, respects every person's Splunk permissions, and keeps your logs in your Splunk.

Description:
TA-sensors brings hardware health monitoring to the machines IPMI can't reach. Consumer desktops, gaming rigs, VMs, SBCs and other BMC-less hosts have no out-of-band management controller, so server-grade hardware telemetry (temperatures, fans, voltages, power) is invisible to Splunk. The Linux kernel already exposes all of it through the hwmon subsystem under /sys/class/hwmon - TA-sensors collects it natively, without a BMC, without ipmitool, and without even the lm-sensors package. Two stdlib-only python3 scripted inputs collect every registered hwmon chip (coretemp/k10temp, acpitz, nvme, r8169, mt7921, amdgpu, vendor drivers, and more): - sensors:status (index=main): one nested-JSON event per cycle with sensor_name, reading, reading_value, units and status for every sensor, including latched _alarm flags. - sensors:metrics (index=metrics): true metric events via METRIC-SCHEMA, named sensors._, ideal for mstats time-series, anomaly alerts and trend dashboards. Milli-scaled sysfs inputs are normalized (temp/in/power/current/humidity /1000, fan raw rpm), duplicate chip names are disambiguated with their hwmon number, and all names are sanitized so metric names stay clean and dashboard-safe. Included dashboards: Sensors Overview (per-host reporting, current readings, alarm table) and Sensors Metrics (CPU cores, temperatures, fans, voltages, power draw, live metric volume). TA-sensors is fully standalone, but pairs with TA-IPMI, which covers BMC-equipped servers - together they give complete hardware observability across a mixed fleet. Free and source-available for personal, educational and evaluation use; commercial use requires a paid license from BentleyPC LLC (see LICENSE).

The add-on runs as a Python 3 modular input on a Splunk Heavy Forwarder. It authenticates to Airtable using a Personal Access Token (PAT) stored securely in Splunk's encrypted credential store (storage/passwords), and polls the Airtable Enterprise Audit Log API on a configurable interval. High-volume, low-security-value event types (such as routine view and login events) are excluded server-side by default before they reach your index, helping control license usage without losing audit-relevant activity. Event category filtering and exclusions are fully configurable per input. Events are indexed with sourcetype airtable:auditlog and mapped toward Splunk CIM-friendly fields, making the data easier to correlate with other audit and identity sources already in your environment. The add-on supports pagination and configurable page size / max-pages-per-run to control API load and indexing volume per polling cycle. This add-on is intended for Splunk admins and security teams who use Airtable as part of their enterprise workflow and need visibility into administrative and security-relevant activity for compliance, insider-risk monitoring, or general operational audit purposes.
